newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end with small gains, M&M net up.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end with small gains, M&M net up.

text.p: Bombay blue chips finished on a strong note on Tuesday, with market spotlight on oil and refinery, and software stocks ahead of an anticipated rise in prices of domestic petroleum products, traders said.
"There was not much movement in the market today, but share prices can be expected to sustain the gains," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Goldman Sachs, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
Bombay's share index ends 26.10 points, or 0.68 percent, higher at a provisional 3,861.45.

Shares of Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) ended 14.25 rupees, or four percent, higher at 358.0 in volumes of 120,501 shares. The company's 1996/97 net profit of 2.09 billion rupees was slightly over market expectations, traders said.
Market attention was focussed on select sectors, with foreign funds keen buyers in oil and refineries and software stocks and select blue chips, participants said.

BPCL rose 18.25 rupees to 405.0, and ONGC 7.25 to 287.75 at the Bombay Exchange. HPCL edged 0.50 rupees lower at 435.25, before jumping to a new 52-week high of 442.0. GAIL shares rose 1.20 rupees to 175.20 at the National Stock Exchange.
Foreign funds were keen bidders in these stocks ahead of Sunday's meeting of the policy-making steering committee of India's ruling United Front, traders said.
The United Front's steering committee has failed to reach any agreement in raising prices at two earlier meetings.
Oil and refinery stocks provide a defensive hedge against the negative influence of any increase in petroleum product prices.

Analysts say the long-delayed oil price hike is necessary if the government is to bridge the oil pool deficit -- the money the government owes oil companies for selling petroleum products well below international rates.
